shared_turn_1.user_message: Why are electronic payments universally trusted, but electronic voting largely viewed as a crazy idea?
shared_turn_1.assistant_response:
Electronic payments are trusted because they’re private, reversible, and auditable: you can check your balance, dispute charges, and institutions reconcile ledgers. Mistakes or fraud are usually detectable and compensable.

Voting needs different guarantees: secrecy, one-person-one-vote, coercion resistance, and public verifiability without revealing how anyone voted. A digital receipt proving your vote was counted can enable coercion or vote-selling evidence. Because a single systemic flaw can invalidate an election, voters demand paper trails and independent audits, which pure e-voting struggles to provide.
